source_audit: R1802 supplies explicit ordinary Frobenius eta-covers for the nonflattening approximate group U and U^6, following the bounded-coordinate refinement and approximate-group covering route used with Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1108.2555, Section 4.1 and Theorem 4.4 (read R1800). It preserves the Haar-ball scale factor and records all polynomial Q losses. This is supporting formalization of known arguments, not a new impossibility theorem. Product growth and its application remain unproved.

proof_scope: In progress. R1802 refines the actual smoothing-scale cover to finite ordinary Frobenius eta-covers of U and U^6. Representatives belong to their respective target sets. The refinement costs at most 1025^4 Q^12 for U and (2^21+1)^4 Q^52 times card(Y)^5 for U^6. Composing with actual nonflattening retains the original geometry, volume and probability conclusions and gives card(E)*q^2*v_eta <= ofReal(1025^4 Q^12)*2^23 K0 L^2 K^20 H(U), and card(E6)*q^2*v_eta <= ofReal((2^21+1)^4 Q^52)*2^68 K0 L^2 K^100 H(U). Here v_eta=H(Ball(eta)). These explicit Q losses introduce no additional explicit inverse-eta power, but Q may itself depend on scale. Near-identity localization, product growth/escape, strict flattening, unconditional gap and paid padding remain unproved. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new transposition bounds.
